label: rare: replaying first token v right after <DEL>, or the token after an "o o" pair
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.006% of steps) with two unrelated parts. (1) About 64% of activation mass, including all of the strongest examples: the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), when the input is the fed-back first token v. It is stronger when the second original token (the current output) is a digit 1-3 or q/p/l/h/k, and when L is short (4-6). (2) About 30% of mass: original-phase steps 2-6 right after two consecutive o inputs ("o o" followed by x). It never fires at t 0-1, at the delimiter, or at copy steps after recall_idx 2. Each part has very low precision: v at recall_idx 1 fires only about 1.4% of the time, and "o o" contexts about 4.6%. So these conditions are necessary-ish context and not sufficient, and the real trigger is some finer conjunction that I could not identify.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=o (+3.15), prev2_tok=o (+3.00), phase=2 & out_tok=1 (+2.90), in_tok=v (+2.89), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=v (+2.54), orig1=o (+2.50). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.98), orig4=1 (-1.56), in_first=0 (-1.15), L=9 (-0.59).
